terms.gloss: anyone you like, anyone at all
evidence: Cic. Phil. 12.5: cujusvīs hominis est errāre
Plaut. Amph. prol. 27: nōn minus quam vostrum quīvīs formīdat malum
terms.comment: Anyone you care to name. After a negative or in a doubting question, “anyone” is quisquam instead (see someone).

terms.gloss: anyone at all, the first who comes
evidence: Ov. Met. 2.388: quīlibet alter agat portantēs lūmina currūs!
Cic. Fin. 3.24: sīc vīta agenda est certō genere quōdam, nōn quōlibet
terms.comment: Often a little slighting: anyone, it does not matter who (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: cujusvīs hominis est errāre; nūllīus nisi īnsipientis persevērāre in errōre
phrases.english: anyone can make a mistake; only a fool persists in one

phrases.latin: etenim ille, cujus hūc jussū veniō, Juppiter nōn minus quam vostrum quīvīs formīdat malum
phrases.english: for the one who sent me here, Jupiter, dreads a beating as much as any of you

sources: Lewis & Short: quivis · Lewis & Short: quilibet
Cicero, Plautus and Ovid checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
